title: Cialis and Alcohol: Is It Safe? Tadalafil Risks and Timing
excerpt: Can you drink on Cialis? How tadalafil and alcohol lower blood pressure together, why the 36-hour window matters, how much is too much, and when to get help.
metaDescription: Can you drink on Cialis? How tadalafil and alcohol lower blood pressure, why the 36-hour window matters, how much is too much, and warning signs.
author: DHM Guide Team
content:
**The honest answer first:** for most healthy men, a drink or two while taking Cialis (tadalafil) is unlikely to cause a problem. The risk climbs with how much you drink. Both alcohol and tadalafil widen your blood vessels and lower your blood pressure a little, and together they can drop it enough to make you dizzy, lightheaded, or faint, especially when you stand up quickly. The Cialis prescribing information specifically warns that drinking substantially (it gives five or more drinks as an example) on tadalafil raises the chance of those effects. There's a second, less obvious problem too: alcohol itself makes erections harder to get and keep, so heavy drinking works against the reason you took the pill in the first place.

**The quick rules:** Keep it to one or two drinks if you've taken Cialis. Remember that tadalafil stays in your body for about a day and a half, so "the Cialis window" includes tomorrow night, not just tonight. Stand up slowly, drink water, and eat. **Never combine Cialis with nitrates**, which includes nitroglycerin for chest pain and the recreational inhalants called "poppers." That combination can cause a dangerous drop in blood pressure, and alcohol only makes it worse.

> **This is not medical advice.** This article explains how the interaction works based on the drug's label and general research. It is not a substitute for a doctor or pharmacist who knows your heart health, blood pressure, and full medication list. **Talk to your doctor before mixing Cialis and alcohol if** you have heart disease, low or high blood pressure, liver or kidney problems, or take an alpha-blocker (such as tamsulosin or doxazosin), blood pressure medicine, or any nitrate. **Get emergency help (call 911 in the US) if** you have chest pain, fainting, an erection lasting more than four hours, or sudden loss of vision or hearing after taking tadalafil. If you have chest pain, tell the paramedics you took Cialis and when.

## How Cialis and Alcohol Interact: The Blood Pressure Effect

Cialis is the brand name for **tadalafil**. It belongs to a group of drugs called **PDE5 inhibitors**, the same family as Viagra (sildenafil) and Levitra (vardenafil). It's prescribed for erectile dysfunction (ED), for the urinary symptoms of an enlarged prostate (benign prostatic hyperplasia, or BPH), and, under a different brand name, for a lung condition called pulmonary arterial hypertension.

Here is what tadalafil does in plain words. Your body uses a signalling molecule called cGMP to tell the smooth muscle in blood vessel walls to relax. An enzyme called PDE5 breaks cGMP down and ends the signal. Tadalafil blocks that enzyme, so the "relax" signal lasts longer. In the penis, that means more blood can flow in during arousal. But PDE5 isn't only found there. It's also in blood vessels elsewhere in the body, which is why tadalafil causes a small, usually unnoticed drop in blood pressure in most people.

Alcohol is also a **vasodilator**, meaning it widens blood vessels. That's why your face can flush and you feel warm after a drink. In the short term, a few drinks can lower blood pressure, especially in the hours after drinking, and alcohol also blunts some of the reflexes that normally keep your blood pressure steady when you stand up.

Put the two together and the effects add up:

- **Both widen blood vessels.** Two mild vasodilators can produce a bigger drop than either alone.
- **Standing up becomes the risky moment.** When you go from lying or sitting to standing, gravity pulls blood toward your legs. Normally your body tightens blood vessels within seconds to compensate. With alcohol and tadalafil on board, that response can lag, and you may feel dizzy or see spots. Doctors call this **orthostatic hypotension**.
- **Your heart tries to make up for it.** A faster heartbeat is a common response when blood pressure dips. Some people notice it as a racing or pounding heart.
- **Dehydration makes it worse.** Alcohol makes you pee more, and less fluid in your blood vessels means lower blood pressure. A night of drinking with not much water is a setup for lightheadedness.

### What the label says

The US prescribing information for Cialis addresses alcohol directly. It describes both alcohol and tadalafil as mild vasodilators and warns that drinking substantially (it gives the example of five or more units) together with Cialis can increase the potential for orthostatic signs and symptoms, including a faster heart rate, a drop in standing blood pressure, dizziness, and headache.

The label also describes studies in healthy volunteers. At moderate amounts of alcohol, tadalafil didn't change how alcohol was absorbed, and alcohol didn't change tadalafil levels in the blood. At higher alcohol doses, some people had drops in blood pressure on standing, and some reported dizziness. In other words, the interaction is about adding together two effects on blood vessels, not one drug changing how the body handles the other.

That matches what most doctors and pharmacists tell patients: **a small amount is generally fine for healthy people, a lot is not.**

## Tadalafil and Alcohol: Why the 36-Hour Window Matters

People searching "tadalafil and alcohol" are often asking the same question as "Cialis and alcohol," since tadalafil is the generic name and generic tadalafil is now widely prescribed. Everything in this article applies equally to brand-name Cialis and generic tadalafil. The drug inside is the same.

What sets tadalafil apart from Viagra is **how long it lasts**. Tadalafil has a half-life of roughly 17.5 hours in healthy men, meaning it takes about that long for half of a dose to leave your body. That's why it can help with erections for up to 36 hours after a dose, which earned it the nickname "the weekend pill." Sildenafil (Viagra), by comparison, has a half-life of about four hours.

That long window is great for spontaneity, but it has a catch with alcohol: **the drug is still active the next day.**

- If you take 20 mg on Friday evening, a meaningful amount is still in your system on Saturday evening.
- If you have a big night out on Saturday, you're drinking on top of tadalafil, even though you took it "yesterday."
- If you take **daily low-dose Cialis** (usually 2.5 mg or 5 mg for ED or BPH), there is always some tadalafil in your blood. There is no tadalafil-free time to save your drinking for.

For daily users, the practical upshot is simple. Your normal drinking habits happen on tadalafil, every time. The daily doses are lower than the as-needed doses, so the blood pressure effect is generally smaller. But the same advice applies: keep it moderate, stay hydrated, and stand up slowly.

### Does the dose change the risk?

In general, higher doses of a PDE5 inhibitor have a larger effect on blood vessels, so a 20 mg dose plus several drinks is more likely to cause dizziness than a 5 mg daily dose plus one beer. The higher daily dose used for pulmonary arterial hypertension (sold as Adcirca and generics) is a different situation. People taking tadalafil for lung blood pressure should ask their specialist about alcohol directly, because their condition and other medicines change the picture.

## Does Alcohol Stop Cialis From Working?

Not chemically. Alcohol doesn't seem to change how tadalafil is absorbed or broken down at moderate amounts, based on the label's description of the volunteer studies. But alcohol has its own effect on erections that tadalafil can't fully override.

Alcohol is a depressant of the central nervous system. It slows the nerve signals between the brain and the body, and it dulls sensation. Arousal and erection rely on those signals. That's why heavy drinking can cause temporary erectile problems even in men without ED, a well-known effect sometimes called "whiskey dick."

Here's how that plays out with Cialis:

- **One or two drinks** may help some people relax and generally don't interfere much with tadalafil's effect.
- **Several drinks** start to dull arousal and sensation. Tadalafil improves blood flow, but it still needs sexual stimulation and working nerve signals to do its job. If alcohol has numbed those, the pill has less to work with.
- **Heavy drinking** can make an erection hard to get or keep even with tadalafil, and it raises the blood pressure risk described above at the same time.

So if you've been told "Cialis doesn't work when I drink," the problem may be the drinking, not the pill. Long term, regular heavy drinking is also linked to erectile dysfunction in its own right, through effects on nerves, blood vessels, hormones (including testosterone), and the liver. If you've noticed ED getting worse alongside regular drinking, that's worth raising with your doctor.

## Side Effects That Alcohol Can Make Worse

Tadalafil's common side effects, according to its label, include headache, indigestion, back pain, muscle aches, flushing, and a stuffy nose. Alcohol overlaps with several of them.

| Tadalafil side effect | How alcohol can add to it |
|---|---|
| Headache | Alcohol widens blood vessels and dehydrates you, both of which can trigger headaches. A tadalafil headache plus a hangover headache is a rough morning. |
| Flushing | Alcohol causes facial flushing in many people, especially those with a sensitivity to it. The two can stack. |
| Indigestion and heartburn | Alcohol relaxes the valve at the top of the stomach and irritates the stomach lining, which makes reflux more likely. |
| Dizziness | The main interaction. Both lower blood pressure, especially on standing. |
| Stuffy nose | Alcohol can cause nasal congestion in some people, partly through blood vessel widening in the nose. |
| Back pain and muscle aches | Not directly worsened by alcohol, but dehydration and poor sleep after drinking can make aches feel worse. |

Most of these are mild and pass on their own. If headaches or dizziness on tadalafil are bothering you, cutting back on alcohol is often the first thing a doctor will suggest.

## The Combinations That Are Actually Dangerous

For a healthy man, Cialis plus a couple of drinks is a low-risk situation. The serious problems come from adding a third thing to the mix.

### Nitrates and poppers: never

**Tadalafil must never be taken with nitrates.** This is the most important safety rule for any PDE5 inhibitor. Nitrates include:

- **Nitroglycerin** (tablets, sprays, or patches for chest pain, also called angina)
- **Isosorbide mononitrate and isosorbide dinitrate**
- **"Poppers,"** inhaled recreational products containing amyl nitrite or related chemicals, sometimes used at parties or during sex

Nitrates and PDE5 inhibitors both act on the same relaxation pathway in blood vessels, and together they can cause a sudden, severe drop in blood pressure that can lead to fainting, heart attack, or stroke. Alcohol lowers blood pressure further. Because tadalafil lasts so long, the label advises that if someone on tadalafil has chest pain and needs nitroglycerin, at least 48 hours should have passed since the last dose, and only under medical supervision. That's why you should always tell paramedics or the emergency room that you take Cialis, and when you last took it.

If poppers are part of your nights out, talk to your doctor honestly before using tadalafil. They've heard it before.

### Alpha-blockers and blood pressure medicines

Many men taking Cialis for BPH are also on an **alpha-blocker** such as tamsulosin (Flomax), alfuzosin, or doxazosin. These also relax blood vessels, and the label advises caution when combining them with tadalafil. Add alcohol and you have three things lowering blood pressure. Men on blood pressure medicines (such as amlodipine, ACE inhibitors, or beta-blockers) face a similar stacking effect. None of these combinations is automatically off-limits, since doctors prescribe them together regularly, but this group should be especially careful with alcohol and ask their doctor what's sensible. Our guide to [alcohol and blood pressure](/never-hungover/alcohol-hypertension-blood-pressure-management-2025) covers how drinking affects blood pressure over time.

### Other drugs that raise tadalafil levels

Tadalafil is broken down in the liver mainly by an enzyme called CYP3A4. Medicines that block that enzyme can raise tadalafil levels in your blood, which strengthens its effects, including the blood pressure drop. Examples listed in the label include some antifungals (such as ketoconazole and itraconazole), some antibiotics (such as clarithromycin), and some HIV medicines (such as ritonavir). Grapefruit juice can also have this effect, and the label notes it may raise tadalafil levels. If you take any of these, your doctor may lower your tadalafil dose, and alcohol becomes a bigger concern.

### Other sedatives and recreational drugs

Alcohol plus other sedating drugs (sleep aids, benzodiazepines, opioids, cannabis) makes falling and poor judgment more likely. Stimulants such as cocaine put extra strain on the heart, which matters for anyone using a drug that affects blood vessels. Our [medication interactions and safety guide](/never-hungover/dhm-medication-interactions-safety-guide-2025) has a broader look at how common medicines interact with alcohol and supplements.

## How Much Alcohol Is OK With Cialis?

There's no single official number that applies to everyone. The label's example of "substantial" drinking is five or more units. Here's a general, practical way to think about it, for healthy adults with no heart disease and no interacting medicines. This is not personal medical advice.

| Situation | General guidance |
|---|---|
| One or two standard drinks with food | Generally considered low risk for healthy men. Stand up slowly and drink water. |
| Three or four drinks | Higher chance of dizziness, headache, and reduced sexual performance. Pace yourself and hydrate. |
| Five or more drinks (binge level) | This is the amount the Cialis label flags. Higher risk of lightheadedness, fainting, and falls. Best avoided on tadalafil. |
| Any alcohol plus nitrates or poppers | Do not combine. Tadalafil and nitrates should never be taken together at all. |
| Heart disease, low blood pressure, or alpha-blockers | Ask your doctor before drinking on tadalafil. |

A standard drink in the US is about 14 grams of alcohol: roughly a 12-ounce beer at 5%, a 5-ounce glass of wine at 12%, or a 1.5-ounce shot of 40% spirits. Many cocktails and craft beers contain more than one standard drink. If you're not sure how long alcohol stays in your body after a night out, our guide on [how long alcohol stays in your system](/never-hungover/how-long-does-alcohol-stay-in-your-system) walks through the timing.

### Practical tips if you're drinking on Cialis

- **Eat a meal.** Food slows how quickly alcohol reaches your blood, which softens the blood pressure dip. Unlike Viagra, tadalafil's absorption isn't meaningfully affected by food, so you don't have to choose between eating and the pill working.
- **Alternate with water.** Staying hydrated keeps your blood volume up.
- **Stand up slowly.** Sit on the edge of the bed for a moment before standing, especially at night or first thing in the morning.
- **Skip the hot tub and sauna after drinking.** Heat widens blood vessels too, which stacks a third vasodilator on top of the other two.
- **Don't double up on pills.** If tadalafil doesn't seem to work after drinking, taking more won't fix the alcohol problem and will raise your risk of side effects. The label says not to take more than one dose a day.

## Cialis vs. Viagra With Alcohol

Both drugs interact with alcohol in the same basic way, by adding to its effect on blood pressure. The differences come from timing.

- **Viagra (sildenafil)** works for about four to five hours and leaves the body relatively quickly. The overlap with a night of drinking is shorter. Its absorption is slowed by a heavy, high-fat meal.
- **Cialis (tadalafil)** lasts up to 36 hours. A dose taken today still overlaps with drinking tomorrow. Food doesn't meaningfully affect it.

Neither one is "safer" with alcohol in any absolute sense. The right choice depends on your health, your other medicines, and your doctor's advice. If you find you only use ED medication on nights you drink heavily, that's a useful thing to bring up at your next appointment.

## When to Get Help Right Away

Most people who mix a little alcohol and tadalafil have no problems at all. But some signs mean you should stop drinking and get medical care.

**Call 911 (US) or go to the emergency room if you have:**

- **Chest pain, pressure, or tightness**, especially during or after sex. Stop sexual activity. Tell the responders you took tadalafil and when, so they don't give you nitroglycerin.
- **Fainting**, or feeling like you're about to pass out and it isn't getting better when you lie down.
- **An erection lasting more than four hours** (priapism). This is a medical emergency that can cause permanent damage if not treated.
- **Sudden loss of vision** in one or both eyes, or **sudden decrease or loss of hearing**, sometimes with ringing in the ears or dizziness. The label lists these as rare but serious effects.
- **Signs of a severe allergic reaction**, such as swelling of the face or throat or trouble breathing.

**Call your doctor soon if you have:**

- Dizziness or lightheadedness that keeps happening when you drink on tadalafil
- A racing or irregular heartbeat
- Headaches that don't go away with rest and fluids
- Worsening erectile problems despite treatment

If someone you're with has drunk a lot, is confused, is vomiting while drowsy, or can't be woken, treat it as a possible case of alcohol poisoning and call 911. That's an emergency regardless of what else they've taken.

## Who Should Be Most Careful

You should talk to your doctor before drinking on tadalafil if you:

- Have **heart disease**, a history of heart attack or stroke, or have been told your heart isn't healthy enough for sex
- Have **low blood pressure**, or **uncontrolled high blood pressure**
- Take **any nitrate**, or use poppers
- Take an **alpha-blocker** for BPH or blood pressure
- Take **multiple blood pressure medicines**
- Have **liver or kidney disease**, which can raise tadalafil levels in the blood
- Are on a medicine that blocks CYP3A4, such as certain antifungals, antibiotics, or HIV drugs
- Are over 65 and prone to dizziness or falls

A pharmacist can review your full medication list in a few minutes, and it's a free conversation at most pharmacies.

## Looking After Yourself the Morning After

If you drank more than you meant to while taking tadalafil, a few simple steps help:

- **Rehydrate steadily.** Water, plus something with electrolytes if you've been sweating or vomiting.
- **Get up slowly.** The morning after is when lightheadedness on standing is most likely, because you're still dehydrated and tadalafil is still active.
- **Eat something gentle.** It helps settle your stomach and blood sugar.
- **Be careful with painkillers.** Ibuprofen and aspirin can irritate a stomach already upset by alcohol, and acetaminophen has its own issues after heavy drinking. Our article on [Tylenol and alcohol](/never-hungover/tylenol-and-alcohol) explains why.
- **Don't take another tadalafil dose** to "fix" anything. One dose a day is the maximum.

The most effective way to avoid a bad morning is still to drink less and pace yourself. Our guide on [how to prevent a hangover](/never-hungover/how-to-prevent-a-hangover) covers the habits with the best evidence.

### What about hangover supplements?

Some people use supplements to support their body on nights they drink. **DHM (dihydromyricetin)** is a plant compound studied for its effects on alcohol metabolism and the liver. Most of the research comes from animal and lab studies, with only limited human data, so it's promising rather than settled. A few honest points for anyone on tadalafil:

- **There's no published research on DHM and tadalafil together.** There is no good evidence either way about how they interact, so ask your doctor or pharmacist before combining them, especially if you're on other medicines too.
- **DHM doesn't change the blood pressure interaction.** Nothing about DHM makes it safer to drink heavily on Cialis, and there is no good evidence that it reduces the dizziness risk.
- **It's not a reason to drink more.** If you do decide to try it after checking with your doctor, well-reviewed options include [Double Wood DHM](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B074N712FM?tag=dhmguide-20) and [No Days Wasted DHM](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0D4BWK6PH?tag=dhmguide-20). Our [DHM dosage guide](/never-hungover/dhm-dosage-guide-2025) covers timing and amounts, and our [supplement reviews](/reviews) compare the main brands.

## The Bottom Line

- Cialis and alcohol both lower blood pressure. A drink or two is generally low risk for healthy men. Heavy drinking (the label uses five or more drinks as its example) raises the risk of dizziness, fainting, headache, and a racing heart.
- Tadalafil lasts up to 36 hours, so drinking the day after a dose still counts. Daily-dose users are always on it.
- Alcohol works against erections on its own, so heavy drinking can make Cialis seem like it isn't working.
- **Never combine tadalafil with nitrates or poppers.** Be extra careful with alpha-blockers and blood pressure medicines.
- Chest pain, fainting, an erection over four hours, or sudden vision or hearing loss means emergency care. Tell responders you took tadalafil.
- When in doubt, talk to your doctor or pharmacist. They can look at your full picture.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Can you drink alcohol while taking Cialis?**

For most healthy men, one or two drinks while taking Cialis is generally considered low risk. Both alcohol and tadalafil lower blood pressure, so drinking heavily (the label gives five or more drinks as an example) raises the chance of dizziness, fainting, headache, and a fast heartbeat. If you have heart disease or low blood pressure, or take alpha-blockers or other blood pressure medicines, ask your doctor before drinking on Cialis.

**Is tadalafil and alcohol the same as Cialis and alcohol?**

Yes. Tadalafil is the generic name for the drug in Cialis, so the interaction is the same whether you take the brand or a generic version. Both widen blood vessels, and together they can lower blood pressure more than either alone, especially when you stand up.

**How long after taking Cialis can I drink?**

Tadalafil has a half-life of roughly 17.5 hours and works for up to 36 hours, so there isn't a short wait that clears it. Drinking the evening after a dose still overlaps with the drug. Daily low-dose users always have some tadalafil in their system. The practical approach is to keep drinking moderate whenever you're within that window, rather than waiting it out.

**Does alcohol make Cialis less effective?**

Alcohol doesn't stop tadalafil from being absorbed at moderate amounts, but it has its own effect on erections. It dulls nerve signals and sensation, so several drinks can make an erection harder to get or keep even with tadalafil. If Cialis seems not to work on nights you drink, the alcohol is the likely cause. Don't take an extra dose; the maximum is one dose a day.

**What happens if you take Cialis and get drunk?**

The main risks are a drop in blood pressure when standing, leading to dizziness, lightheadedness, or fainting, plus a faster heartbeat and a worse headache. Sexual performance is also likely to suffer. Sit or lie down if you feel faint, drink water, and get up slowly. Seek emergency care for chest pain, fainting that doesn't resolve, an erection lasting over four hours, or sudden vision or hearing loss.

**Can I take Cialis with poppers or nitroglycerin if I've been drinking?**

No. Tadalafil should never be combined with nitrates, including nitroglycerin and recreational poppers (amyl nitrite), with or without alcohol. The combination can cause a sudden, dangerous drop in blood pressure. Because tadalafil lasts so long, the label advises at least 48 hours between a dose and any nitrate, and only under medical supervision. If you have chest pain, tell emergency responders you took tadalafil.

**Is Cialis or Viagra safer with alcohol?**

Both interact with alcohol in the same way, by adding to its blood-pressure-lowering effect. Viagra (sildenafil) wears off in a few hours, while Cialis lasts up to 36 hours, so Cialis overlaps with more drinking occasions. Neither is safe to mix with heavy drinking. Which one suits you best depends on your health and other medicines, so ask your doctor.

**Can I take DHM with Cialis?**

There is no published research on DHM and tadalafil together, so there is no good evidence either way about how they interact. DHM does not reduce the blood pressure risk of drinking on Cialis. Ask your doctor or pharmacist before combining them, especially if you take other medicines.
